items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Ellington was the worst. And as well as I knew him, and I knew I’d be a better guest talking about him than he was.

ctx.x: It’s kind of a high pressure situation, every day having to come up with something fresh I would think.

Yes, absolutely. And the reading of course was a killer, because Arlene never had time to do anything, so I did all the reading. And it got so toward the end that I would say to the publishers, because they knew that we sold books. We had the number one rating on the air and the station was easy to find, right in the middle of the dial, and the loudest station on the dial. And so they’d say, “Oh Jean, this is right up your alley. This book is marvelous. It’s an overview of—” I’d say, “what’s the magic number?” If…
“it wasn’t only Arlene, it was Ellington. The two of them were jiving each other and you didn’t get anything. It was not one of his finer moments.
